He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Wagner Seahawks men's basketball|Wagner Seahawks]] and the [[Richmond Spiders men's basketball|Richmond Spiders]]. ==High school career== After spending his freshman year at [[Bishop O'Connell High School]] in [[Arlington County, Virginia|Arlington, Virginia]], Francis transferred to [[Westfield High School (Virginia)|Westfield High School]] in [[Chantilly, Virginia]].{{cite news |last1=Parker |first1=Brandon |title=Westfield's Blake Francis emerges as standout on young team |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/recruiting-insider/wp/2014/02/18/westfields-blake-francis-emerges-as-standout-on-young-team/ |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |accessdate=October 7, 2020 |date=February 18, 2014}} As a senior, he averaged 20.1 points per game and led Westfield to the Virginia 6A state championship, scoring 23 points against [[Oscar F. Smith High School]] in the title game.{{cite web |last1=O'Connor |first1=John |title=Transfer guard Blake Francis has connections that helped him hook up with Spiders |url=https://richmond.com/sports/college/schools/university-richmond/transfer-guard-blake-francis-has-connections-that-helped-him-hook-up-with-spiders/article_30d28dc7-d358-50ca-9465-e974ee013322.html |website=[[Richmond Times-Dispatch]] |accessdate=October 7, 2020 |date=April 11, 2018}}{{cite web |title=Blake Francis |url=https://richmondspiders.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/blake-francis/4057 |website=University of Richmond Athletics |accessdate=October 7, 2020}} He was a Second Team All-State selection.{{cite web |last1=O'Connor |first1=John |title=Blake Francis has already been a Division I star, at Wagner. His new goal: help the Spiders win. |url=https://richmond.com/sports/college/plus/blake-francis-has-already-been-a-division-i-star-at/article_a810ac64-19d4-57e6-9450-f01bdea531e4.html |website=[[Richmond Times-Dispatch]] |accessdate=October 7, 2020 |date=October 31, 2019}} Francis left as Westfield's all-time leading scorer, with 1,390 career points. He planned to attend [[College-preparatory school|prep school]] because he had no [[NCAA Division I]] scholarship offers. He accepted an offer from [[Wagner Seahawks men's basketball|Wagner]] when a scholarship suddenly became available on the team because two-sport athlete [[Greg Senat]] had switched his scholarship from basketball to [[American football|football]].{{cite web |last1=Kussoy |first1=Howie |title=Wagner sophomore star won't go overlooked again |url=https://nypost.com/2017/12/15/wagner-sophomore-star-wont-go-overlooked-again/ |website=[[New York Post]] |accessdate=October 7, 2020 |date=December 15, 2017}}{{cite web |title=Blake Francis |url=https://wagnerathletics.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/blake-francis/8904 |website=Wagner College Athletics |accessdate=October 7, 2020}} ==College career== As a freshman at Wagner, Francis averaged 7.2 points per game in a [[Substitution (sport)|reserve]] role. Due to the departures of important players after the season, he was given more opportunities as a sophomore.{{cite web |last1=O'Connor |first1=John |title=Spider Blake Francis' decision to transfer from Wagner looks better every day |url=https://richmond.com/sports/college/plus/spider-blake-francis-decision-to-transfer-from-wagner-looks-better-every-day/article_5b376d9b-7605-5124-b429-b7286e7b2d14.html |website=[[Richmond Times-Dispatch]] |accessdate=October 7, 2020 |date=July 30, 2020}} On February 8, 2018, Francis scored a career-high 29 points in a 96–76 win over [[Bryant Bulldogs men's basketball|Bryant]].{{cite web |title=First-Place Seahawks Soar Past Bryant 96–76 For Seventh Straight Win, Improving To 13–0 At Home |url=https://wagnerathletics.com/news/2018/2/8/mens-basketball-first-place-seahawks-soar-past-bryant-96-76-for-seventh-straight-improving-to-13-0-at-home.aspx |website=Wagner College Athletics |accessdate=October 7, 2020 |date=February 8, 2018}} In his sophomore season, he averaged 17.3 points per game and made a program-record 102 three-pointers. Francis was named to the Second Team All-[[Northeast Conference]]. He transferred to [[Richmond Spiders men's basketball|Richmond]] and sat out his next year per [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] rules.{{cite web |title=All-NEC Performer Blake Francis Will Transfer To Richmond |url=https://richmondspiders.com/news/2018/4/10/mens-basketball-all-nec-performer-blake-francis-will-transfer-to-richmond |website=University of Richmond Athletics |accessdate=October 7, 2020 |date=April 10, 2018}} He was drawn to Richmond because his friend Cedrick Lindsay had played there and some of his former [[Amateur Athletic Union]] teammates were on the roster. During his [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] year, he recovered from foot surgery. On December 3, 2019, Francis matched his career-high of 29 points, shooting 6-of-9 from three-point range, in an 80–63 victory over [[Hampton Pirates men's basketball|Hampton]].{{cite web |title=Francis scores 29 to carry Richmond over Hampton 80–63 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story?id=28221690 |website=[[ESPN]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |accessdate=October 7, 2020 |date=December 3, 2019}} On January 11, 2020, he suffered a [[sternal fracture]] when diving for a loose ball during a 75–58 loss against [[Saint Louis Billikens men's basketball|Saint Louis]] and was expected to miss four to six weeks.{{cite web |title=Richmond leading scorer Blake Francis out 4–6 weeks |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/28495750/richmond-leading-scorer-blake-francis-4-6-weeks |website=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=October 7, 2020 |date=January 16, 2020}} He returned to action against [[Fordham Rams men's basketball|Fordham]] on February 8 and finished with 18 points.{{cite web |last1=O'Connor |first1=John |title=Blake Francis' handspring at La Salle was fine sign for UR as it preps for rematch vs. VCU |url=https://richmond.com/sports/college/plus/blake-francis-handspring-at-la-salle-was-fine-sign-for-ur-as-it-preps-for/article_1a6ca27d-e051-5eed-9813-51eed29273b6.html |website=[[Richmond Times-Dispatch]] |accessdate=October 7, 2020 |date=February 13, 2020}} As a junior, Francis led the team in scoring with 17.7 points per game while also averaging 2.2 rebounds and 2 assists per game. He earned Second Team All-[[Atlantic 10 Conference|Atlantic 10]] honors.{{cite news |last1=Hajduczka |first1=Krystian |title=Three Richmond men's basketball players declare for the 2020 NBA Draft |url=https://www.thecollegianur.com/article/2020/04/richmond-basketball-players-declaring-for-nba-draft |accessdate=October 8, 2020 |work=The Collegian |date=April 7, 2020}} He led Richmond to a program-record 14 conference wins. Francis declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]] before withdrawing his name and opting to return to Richmond.{{cite web |title=Francis, Gilyard, Golden Officially Withdraw From NBA Draft |url=https://richmondspiders.com/news/2020/6/3/mens-basketball-francis-gilyard-golden-officially-withdraw-from-nba-draft.aspx |website=University of Richmond Athletics |accessdate=October 7, 2020 |date=June 3, 2020}} After the 2020–21 season, Francis declined to take an additional year of eligibility granted to all players, instead opting for the [[2021 NBA draft]].{{cite news|title=Richmond's Blake Francis declares for 2021 NBA Draft|url=https://augustafreepress.com/richmonds-blake-francis-declares-for-2021-nba-draft/|date=April 13, 2020|access-date=April 25, 2021|work=Augusta Free Press|archive-date=April 25, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210425125158/https://augustafreepress.com/richmonds-blake-francis-declares-for-2021-nba-draft/|url-status=dead}} ==Professional career== ===Westchester Knicks (2021–2022)=== Francis was drafted second round (15th pick overall) by the [[Raptors 905]] in the [[2021 NBA G League draft|2021 NBA G League Draft]].{{Cite web|title=2021 NBA G League Draft Board|url=https://gleague.nba.com/2021-nba-g-league-draft-order/|access-date=2021-10-23|website=NBA G League|language=en-US}} However, he did not make the team's final roster. On December 30, 2021, Francis was acquired by the [[Westchester Knicks]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021-22 NBA G League Transactions|date=December 30, 2021|access-date=December 30, 2021}} Francis was then later waived on January 26, 2022.{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021-22 NBA G League Transactions|date=January 26, 2022|access-date=January 26, 2022}} On February 8, 2022, Francis was acquired by the Raptors 905, but was waived on February 10. ===Capital City Go-Go (2022)=== On March 9, Francis was acquired and activated by the [[Capital City Go-Go]] off of waivers. He was later waived on November 14, 2022, and then re-acquired on December 3, and then waived again on December 9, 2022.{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/22-23-nba-g-league-transactions|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2022-23 NBA G League Transactions|date=November 14, 2022|access-date=November 14, 2022}}{{cite February 11, 2023, Francis was acquired by the [[Cleveland Charge]].{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/22-23-nba-g-league-transactions|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2022-23 NBA G League Transactions|date=February 11, 2023|access-date=February 11, 2023}} ===Montreal Alliance (2023)=== On May 4, 2023, Francis signed with the [[Montreal Alliance]] of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball playing 7 games for the club.{{cite web|title=Canadian shooting guard Negus Webster-Chan signs with Montréal
